## The trap (live, EI-395, 2026-06-13)

`fleet:assignments` flagged the `improvement-runner` routine's parked claims as
orphaned (a live lease whose holder never heartbeats), which nearly bulk-swept
the paused improvement-implement lane. A prior agent "fixed" it by **editing the
already-applied migration** `225-fleet-assignment-nursery-alias-liveness.sql`
in place — adding `AND owner NOT IN ('improvement-runner')` to the view's
`orphaned` clause (committed 02:20). The fix looked done: the file was correct,
and a fresh-DB integration test (which builds the schema from all `sql/*.sql`)
would go green.

But the **live DB never changed.** Migration 225 was applied days earlier and is
recorded in `harness_shared.schema_migrations`; the boot-apply / deploy runner
**skips files already in that ledger by filename**. Editing the body of an
applied migration is a no-op on every existing DB. `pg_get_viewdef` confirmed the
live view still had the un-excluded `orphaned` clause and improvement-runner's 48
claims still read `orphaned=true`.

## The rule

To change a view (or any DDL) that a prior migration already defined:

1. **Reserve a new number** — `db:next-migration` (races-safe; never `ls | tail`).
2. **Write a new `sql/<NNN>` with `CREATE OR REPLACE VIEW …`** carrying the full,
   current view body. The latest migration is the single owner of the view def.
3. **Revert the in-place edit** to the old migration so it stays faithful to what
   it applied (and so two files don't both claim to own the view). Fresh installs
   then run old-then-new and converge; existing DBs get the new one only.
4. **`pull-schema`** (`libs/papercusp/libs/db/scripts/pull-schema.mjs`) to refresh
   `generated.ts`. A view change touches only the view's `.as(sql\`…\`)` block —
   revert any unrelated drift (e.g. an index opclass flip) pull-schema also picks up.

## Verify against the LIVE DB, not the file

The file is not the source of truth for a running system — the catalog is:

```bash
PGPASSWORD=harness_admin_pwd psql -U harness_admin -h localhost -d papercusp -tAc \
  "SELECT pg_get_viewdef('harness_shared.fleet_assignment'::regclass);"
```

(`postgresql://harness_admin:harness_admin_pwd@localhost:5432/papercusp` is the
dev-box native fallback — `embedded-pg-discovery.ts` `NATIVE_FALLBACK`.) Grepping
the migration file, or even grepping the viewdef for a string that lives in a
comment, will lie to you — read the actual computed clause / a representative row.

## Applying it live

`db:migrate { confirm:true }` drains correctly but reports `applied:false` unless
`PAPERCUSP_ALLOW_DB_MIGRATE=1` is set in the serving operator's env (the dev box
doesn't). See [staging-restart-does-not-boot-apply-migrations](/internal/docs/agent-insights/staging-restart-does-not-boot-apply-migrations)
for the blessed direct path (`applyPendingMigrations` from
`@papercusp/embedded-postgres-server` — idempotent, ledger-recording, NOT raw
`psql -f`). If you do fall back to `psql -f`, INSERT the `schema_migrations` row
(filename + `sha256sum` of the file + `now()`) in the **same transaction**, or
the deploy re-runs it — and a re-run of un-guarded `GRANT`/`ALTER`/`POLICY` DDL
can hit `lock_timeout` and roll back the whole deploy (see
[migration-reapply-lock-guards](/internal/docs/agent-insights/migration-reapply-lock-guards)).
A `CREATE OR REPLACE VIEW` body is idempotent, so a recorded re-run is harmless.
